lines: 8 fade channels, each taking a stereo pair of signals and fading them up or down on a curve you set
The left signal of that fade channel, multiplied by the channel's fade level on its way to the L output; a polyphonic cable is summed to one channel first
The right signal of that fade channel, multiplied by the channel's fade level on its way to the R output; a polyphonic cable is summed to one channel first
A rising edge past 0.01V flips that channel's button, so a channel that was fading in starts fading out and one that was out starts fading in
Flips that channel between fading in and fading out; it latches, and the channel stays open for as long as it is on
The time a fade in takes, 0.05 to 100 seconds and 20 seconds on arrival; a higher setting gives a longer fade, despite the column being marked Speed
The time a fade out takes, 0.05 to 100 seconds and 20 seconds on arrival; a higher setting gives a longer fade, despite the column being marked Speed
Bends the fade curve, -1 to 3, with 0 a straight line; below 0 the level climbs early in a fade in, above 0 it stays low until the end. Default -0.7
The L input of that channel scaled by its fade level; with nothing patched to that input the jack carries the fade shape itself, 0V to 10V
The R input of that channel scaled by its fade level; with nothing patched to that input the jack carries the fade shape itself, 0V to 10V
Note — every channel arrives faded out and passes nothing. Press a channel's button, or send a rising edge to its trigger jack, to fade it in.
Note — the number readout shows the value of the Speed knob last turned. The Slope knobs do not write to it, so it shows a fade time and nothing else.

The lines follow the code. Nothing is written to an output pair while both of its jacks are unpatched (:278).

lines: A five-row precision CV adder after the Doepfer A-185-2, each row added to, subtracted from or left out of a running total, with that total and its inverse on two jacks
The CV of the first row, which reaches the output whatever its MODE switch is set to; the switch governs only whether the V knob's voltage joins it
A CV added to or subtracted from the total according to that row's MODE switch; with nothing patched the row offers a flat 1V instead, so the switch transposes by an octave
Chooses what the V knob's voltage does to the first CV IN: + adds it, - subtracts it, 0 leaves it out
Chooses what that row does to the total: + adds its CV, - subtracts its CV, 0 leaves the row out
Scales the volt that the first row's MODE switch adds or subtracts, 0 to 1V, so the first input can be trimmed by a fraction of an octave. Default 1, a whole volt
Sets that row's MODE switch from a voltage: above 0V selects +, below 0V selects -, and only an exact 0V selects the middle position
The running total of the rows their MODE switches admit
The running total of the rows their MODE switches admit, with its sign flipped
Note — a voltage at a MODE CV jack is written straight into the switch, so the switch moves on the panel and stays wherever the CV last left it after the cable is pulled.
Note — a row with nothing patched to its CV IN contributes anyway, a whole volt in the direction its MODE switch points, except the first row, which contributes the V knob's voltage instead.

htAdder.notes: The MODE CV jacks do not add to the switches, they assign to them: params[PARAM_ADDER_MODE + ch].value is set to -1, 0 or 1 at src/htAdder.cpp:154-159. The switch therefore moves on the panel and keeps the position the CV last wrote once the cable is removed. The middle position needs an exact 0.0f, which a continuous CV will rarely hit. The first row is not like the other four: at :173 its CV is assigned to the total rather than added, and it is assigned whether or not the switch is at 0, so setting that switch to 0 does not remove the row. All ten jacks are read through Port::value, which is channel 0 of a polyphonic cable.
